source_text: Ὅσοι οὖν ἐκ Πνεύματος ἁγίου ἐγεννήθησαν, οὗτοι ἐκ Θεοῦ ἐγεννήθησαν. Καὶ ὅσοι εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθησαν, οὗτοι εἰς Πατέρα καὶ ἅγιον Πνεῦμα ἐβαπτίσθησαν. Καὶ πάλιν, ὅτε λέγει ὁ Πέτρος τῷ Ἀνανίᾳ· Διὰ τί ἐπλήρωσεν ὁ Σατανᾶς τὴν καρδίαν σου, ψεύσασθαί σε τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, καὶ νοσφίσασθαι ἀπὸ τῆς τιμῆς τοῦ χωρίου; Οὐκ ἐψεύσω ἀνθρώποις, ἀλλὰ τῷ Θεῷ. Ὥστε ὁ ψευσάμενος τῷ ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι, τῷ Θεῷ ἐψεύσατο, τῷ κατοικοῦντι ἐν ἀνθρώποις διὰ τοῦ Πνεύματος αὐτοῦ. 1008 Ὅπου γάρ ἐστι τὸ Πνεῦμα τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἐκεῖ ἐστιν ὁ Θεός· Ἐν τούτῳ γὰρ, φησὶ, γινώσκομεν, ὅτι ὁ Θεὸς ἐν ἡμῖν μένει, ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ Πνεύματος αὐτοῦ δέδωκεν ἡμῖν Καὶ ὅτε μὲν λέγει ἡ Γραφὴ, ὅτι Πνεῦμα ἅγιον ἐλάλει ἐν τοῖς προφήταις, ἀλλαχοῦ λέγει ὁ μακάριος Παῦλος, ὅτι ὁ Πατὴρ ἐλάλει ἐν τοῖς προφήταις· Πολυμερῶς γὰρ καὶ πολυτρόπως πάλαι ὁ Θεὸς λαλήσας τοῖς πατράσιν ἐν τοῖς προφήταις, ἐπ' ἐσχάτου τοῦ ἡμερῶν τούτων ἐλάλησεν ἡμῖν ἐν Υἱῷ. Καὶ ἀλλαχοῦ λέγει, ὅτι ὁ Υἱὸς λαλεῖ· Εἰ δοκιμὴν, φησὶ, ζητεῖτε τοῦ ἐν ἐμοὶ λαλοῦντος Χριστοῦ. Ὁ δὲ Υἱὸς τὸ Πνεῦμα εἶπε τὸ λαλοῦν ἐν τοῖς ἀποστόλοις, Ὅταν, φησὶ, παραδώσουσιν ὑμᾶς εἰς συνέδρια, μὴ μεριμνήσητε, πῶς, ἢ τί λαλήσητε· δοθήσεται γὰρ ὑμῖν ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ, τί λαλήσητε. Οὐ γὰρ ὑμεῖς ἐστε οἱ λαλοῦντες, ἀλλὰ τὸ Πνεῦμα τοῦ Πατρὸς ὑμῶν, τὸ λαλοῦν ἐν ὑμῖν. Καὶ ὁτὲ μὲν ὁ Ἀπόστολος λέγει, ὅτι τὰ σώματα τῶν πιστῶν ναός ἐστι τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος, ὁτὲ δὲ τὰ μέλη αὐτῶν μέλη Χριστοῦ, ὁτὲ δὲ αὐτοὺς ναὸν εἶναι τοῦ Πατρός· Ὑμεῖς γὰρ, φησὶ, ναός ἐστε Θεοῦ ζῶντος, καθὼς εἶπεν ὁ Θεός· Ἐνοικήσω ἐν αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἐμπεριπατήσω, καὶ ἔσομαι αὐτοῖς Θεὸς, καὶ αὐτοὶ ἔσονταί μου λαός· καὶ, Εἴ τις φθείρῃ τὸν ναὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ, φθερεῖ τοῦτον ὁ Θεός. Καὶ πάλιν· Οὐκ οἴδατε, ὅτι ναὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐστε, καὶ τὸ Πνεῦμα τοῦ Θεοῦ τὸ ἅγιον οἰκεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν; Εἴ τις γάρ ἐστι ναὸς τοῦ Πνεύματος, οὗτος ναός ἐστι τοῦ Υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ Πατρός· ὅπου γὰρ τὸ Πνεῦμα τοῦ Θεοῦ κατοικεῖ, ἐκεῖ ὁ Θεὸς κατοικεῖ. Καὶ, Ὥσπερ ὁ Πατὴρ ἐγείρει τοὺς νεκροὺς καὶ ζωοποιεῖ, οὕτως καὶ ὁ Υἱὸς οὓς θέλει ζωοποιεῖ. Ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ περὶ τοῦ Πνεύματος λέγει, ὅτι Τὸ Πνεῦμά ἐστι τὸ ζωοποιοῦν, ἡ σὰρξ οὐκ ὠφελεῖ οὐδέν. Πρὸς δὲ Κορινθίους γράφει Παῦλος· Τὸ δὲ Πνεῦμα ζωοποιεῖ. Ὁρᾷς, ὅτι ἅπερ ἐστὶν ἔργα τοῦ Πατρὸς, ταῦτα λέγει ἡ Γραφὴ τοῦ Υἱοῦ εἶναι, καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος· ὡς καὶ ὁ Ἀπόστολος ἐδίδαξε λέγων· Διαιρέσεις δὲ χαρισμάτων εἰσὶ, τὸ δὲ Πνεῦμα τὸ αὐτό· καὶ διαιρέσεις δια 1009 κονιῶν εἰσι, καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ Κύριος· καὶ διαιρέσεις ἐνεργημάτων εἰσὶν, ὁ δὲ αὐτὸς Θεὸς ὁ ἐνεργῶν τὰ πάντα ἐν πᾶσι. Εἰρηκὼς οὖν, ὅτι ὁ Πατήρ ἐστιν ὁ ἐνεργῶν τὰ πάντα ἐν πᾶσι, καὶ μετ' ὀλίγον λέγει τὸ ἅγιον Πνεῦμα εἶναι τὸ ἐνεργοῦν τὰ πάντα ἐν πᾶσι.
thought_title: The Spirit's works are the Father's and the Son's
orientation: Marcellus is arguing that the Holy Spirit is uncreated and fully divine by showing that Scripture assigns the same works—indwelling, speaking in prophets, raising the dead—to Father, Son, and Spirit alike.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore as many as were born of the Holy Spirit, these were born of God. And as many as were baptized into Christ, these were baptized into the Father and the Holy Spirit. And again, when Peter says to Ananias: Why did Satan fill your heart, for you to lie to the Holy Spirit, and to keep back from the price of the field? You have not lied to human beings, but to God. So the one who lied to the Holy Spirit lied to God, to the one dwelling in human beings through his Spirit. For where the Spirit of God is, there God is. For in this, he says, we know that God remains in us, because he has given us of his Spirit. And when the Scripture says that the Holy Spirit was speaking in the prophets, elsewhere the blessed Paul says that the Father was speaking in the prophets: For in many parts and in many ways long ago God, having spoken to the fathers in the prophets, in the last of these days spoke to us in the Son. And elsewhere he says that the Son speaks: If, he says, you seek proof of Christ speaking in me. And the Son said the Spirit is the one speaking in the apostles: Whenever, he says, they hand you over to councils, do not be anxious how or what you will say; for it will be given to you in that hour what you will say. For you are not the ones speaking, but the Spirit of your Father, the one speaking in you. And at one time the Apostle says that the bodies of the faithful are a temple of the Holy Spirit, at another time that their members are members of Christ, at another time that they are a temple of the Father: For you, he says, are a temple of the living God, just as God said: I will dwell in them, and I will walk among them, and I will be God to them, and they will be my people; and, If anyone destroys the temple of God, God will destroy this one. And again: Do you not know that you are a temple of God, and the Holy Spirit of God dwells in you? For if anyone is a temple of the Spirit, this one is a temple of the Son and of the Father; for where the Spirit of God dwells, there God dwells. And, Just as the Father raises the dead and gives life, so also the Son gives life to whom he wills. And likewise also concerning the Spirit he says, that The Spirit is the one giving life, the flesh profits nothing. And to the Corinthians Paul writes: And the Spirit gives life. You see, that whatever are works of the Father, these the Scripture says are of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit; as also the Apostle taught saying: And there are varieties of gifts, but the same Spirit; and there are varieties of ministries, and the same Lord; and there are varieties of workings, but the same God working all things in all. Having said therefore, that the Father is the one working all things in all, and after a little he says the Holy Spirit is the one working all things in all.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'temple' for ναός, used here of believers as the dwelling place of God through the Spirit.
The verb is used of Father, Son, and Spirit to show their shared divine work; 'gives life' keeps the active force of the Greek.
The phrase is repeated for Father and Spirit to show the same divine operation; the literal rendering preserves the parallel.

choices.term: νοσφίσασθαι ἀπὸ τῆς τιμῆς τοῦ χωρίου
choices.english: to keep back from the price of the field
choices.why: The infinitive of purpose after 'filled your heart' is kept as an infinitive in English to preserve the syntax of the accusation.
rejected: to embezzle from the price of the land
to pilfer from the proceeds of the property

choices.english: in many parts and in many ways
choices.why: The adverbial pair is rendered literally to preserve the rhetorical force of the quotation from Hebrews.
rejected: at many times and in various manners

pass_b_english: So all who have been born of the Holy Spirit have been born of God. And all who have been baptized into Christ have been baptized into the Father and the Holy Spirit. Again, when Peter says to Ananias, “Why has Satan filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit and to keep back from the price of the field? You have not lied to men but to God” (Acts 5:3–4), it follows that the one who lied to the Holy Spirit lied to God, who dwells in human beings through his Spirit. For where the Spirit of God is, there God is. “By this,” he says, “we know that God abides in us, because he has given us of his Spirit” (1 John 4:13).

And when Scripture says that the Holy Spirit spoke in the prophets, elsewhere the blessed Paul says that the Father spoke in the prophets: “In many parts and in many ways God spoke of old to the fathers in the prophets, but in these last days he has spoken to us in a Son” (Hebrews 1:1–2). And elsewhere he says that the Son speaks: “If you seek proof,” he says, “of Christ speaking in me” (2 Corinthians 13:3). But the Son said that the Spirit is the one speaking in the apostles: “When they hand you over to councils, do not be anxious how or what you will say; for what you will say will be given to you in that hour. For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father speaking in you” (Matthew 10:19–20).

And at one time the Apostle says that the bodies of believers are a temple of the Holy Spirit, at another that their members are members of Christ, and at another that they are a temple of the Father: “For you are the temple of the living God, as God said: ‘I will dwell in them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people’” (2 Corinthians 6:16); and, “If anyone destroys the temple of God, God will destroy him” (1 Corinthians 3:17). And again: “Do you not know that you are the temple of God, and that the Holy Spirit of God dwells in you?” (1 Corinthians 3:16). For if anyone is a temple of the Spirit, he is a temple of the Son and of the Father; for where the Spirit of God dwells, there God dwells.

And, “As the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so also the Son gives life to whom he wills” (John 5:21). Likewise he says about the Spirit, “It is the Spirit that gives life; the flesh profits nothing” (John 6:63). And Paul writes to the Corinthians, “The Spirit gives life” (2 Corinthians 3:6). Do you see that the works which are the Father’s, Scripture says are also the Son’s and the Holy Spirit’s? So also the Apostle taught when he said, “There are varieties of gifts, but the same Spirit; and there are varieties of ministries, and the same Lord; and there are varieties of workings, but the same God who works all things in all” (1 Corinthians 12:4–6). Having said, then, that the Father is the one who works all things in all, a little later he says that the Holy Spirit is the one who works all things in all.

last_rejected.quote: You have not lied to men but to God
last_rejected.source_quote: Οὐκ ἐψεύσω ἀνθρώποις, ἀλλὰ τῷ Θεῷ
last_rejected.why: Wrong tense: ἐψεύσω is aorist indicative 'you lied,' not perfect 'you have lied.'
last_rejected.fix: You lied not to men but to God.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐψεύσω is aorist, but 'you lied' vs 'you have lied' is normal English range, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: who dwells in human beings through his Spirit
last_rejected.source_quote: τῷ κατοικοῦντι ἐν ἀνθρώποις διὰ τοῦ Πνεύματος αὐτοῦ
last_rejected.why: Missing 'his' before Spirit: διὰ τοῦ Πνεύματος αὐτοῦ means 'through his Spirit.'
last_rejected.fix: who dwells in human beings through his Spirit.
last_rejected.ruling: αὐτοῦ is rendered 'his' earlier in the sentence; 'through his Spirit' is clearly intended, not a real omission.

last_rejected.quote: he has given us of his Spirit
last_rejected.source_quote: ἐκ τοῦ Πνεύματος αὐτοῦ δέδωκεν ἡμῖν
last_rejected.why: Wrong pronoun: φησὶ refers to John, not God; 'he' should be 'we' or restructured.
last_rejected.fix: "By this," he says, "we know that God abides in us, because from his Spirit he has given to us."
last_rejected.ruling: φησὶ is a quotative particle; 'he says' is standard rendering. Pronoun reference is a preference, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: God spoke of old to the fathers in the prophets
last_rejected.source_quote: ὁ Θεὸς λαλήσας τοῖς πατράσιν ἐν τοῖς προφήταις
last_rejected.why: Wrong syntax: λαλήσας is aorist participle 'having spoken,' not finite verb; 'God' is object of preceding preposition.
last_rejected.fix: God having spoken of old to the fathers in the prophets.
last_rejected.ruling: λαλήσας is aorist participle, but 'God spoke' correctly renders the sense in the Hebrews quotation. Not a major error.

last_rejected.why: Wrong person: ζητεῖτε is second person plural 'you [plural] seek,' but Paul is addressing Corinthians, not readers directly.
last_rejected.fix: "If," he says, "you seek proof of Christ speaking in me."
last_rejected.ruling: ζητεῖτε is 2nd plural 'you seek'; Paul addresses the Corinthians directly. 'You seek' is correct, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: what you will say will be given to you
last_rejected.source_quote: δοθήσεται γὰρ ὑμῖν ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ, τί λαλήσητε
last_rejected.why: Wrong word order and emphasis: τί λαλήσητε is 'what you will say,' but it comes after 'in that hour,' making it 'for in that hour what you will say will be given to you.'
last_rejected.fix: for in that hour what you will say will be given to you.
last_rejected.ruling: Word order difference in English vs Greek is a preference, not a major error. Meaning is preserved.

last_rejected.quote: the Spirit of your Father speaking in you
last_rejected.source_quote: τὸ Πνεῦμα τοῦ Πατρὸς ὑμῶν, τὸ λαλοῦν ἐν ὑμῖν
last_rejected.why: Missing 'your' clarity: τοῦ Πατρὸς ὑμῶν is 'your Father,' but 'speaking' obscures that this is a relative clause 'which speaks.'
last_rejected.fix: but the Spirit of your Father, which speaks in you.
last_rejected.ruling: 'The Spirit of your Father speaking in you' correctly renders τὸ Πνεῦμα τοῦ Πατρὸς ὑμῶν τὸ λαλοῦν ἐν ὑμῖν. No major error.

last_rejected.quote: If anyone destroys the temple of God, God will destroy him
last_rejected.source_quote: Εἴ τις φθείρῃ τὸν ναὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ, φθερεῖ τοῦτον ὁ Θεός
last_rejected.why: Wrong verb: φθείρῃ/φθερεῖ means 'corrupts/will corrupt,' not 'destroys/destroy.'
last_rejected.fix: If anyone corrupts the temple of God, God will corrupt him.
last_rejected.ruling: φθείρω includes 'destroy' in its semantic range; standard translations render it 'destroys.' Not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: the works which are the Father's, Scripture says are also the Son's and the Holy Spirit's
last_rejected.source_quote: ἅπερ ἐστὶν ἔργα τοῦ Πατρὸς, ταῦτα λέγει ἡ Γραφὴ τοῦ Υἱοῦ εἶναι, καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος
last_rejected.why: Wrong structure: τοῦ Υἱοῦ εἶναι means 'to be the Son's,' not 'are also the Son's'; the 'also' is added.
last_rejected.fix: the works which are the Father's, Scripture says these are the Son's and the Holy Spirit's.
last_rejected.ruling: Adding 'also' reflects the καί in the Greek (τοῦ Υἱοῦ εἶναι, καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος). Not a major error.
